match.reason: No existing point covers operations performance objectives and the trade-offs between them, so this needs a new point.

draft.title: Performance objectives
card: Performance objectives are the goals an operations team sets for how well it makes goods or delivers services. They are quality, speed, dependability, flexibility, customisation and low cost.
the product or service meets what the customer expects. Speed is how quickly the customer gets it. Dependability is delivering on time, every time.
the ability to change the volume or timing of output. Customisation is changing the product to suit each customer. Low cost means keeping the cost of each item down.
Improving one objective often costs another. For example, a business that customises each order may find its cost per item rises. A business must decide which objectives matter most to its customers.
draft.remember: Operations has six objectives, and a gain in one can come at the expense of another.

a.q: Which objective is a business working on when it promises to deliver every order on the day it said it would?
opts: Dependability
Speed
Flexibility
Customisation
a.why: Dependability is about delivering on time, every time. Speed is tempting, but it is about how fast the customer gets the product, not whether the promised time is kept.
a.clue: The focus is on keeping a promise, not on how fast.

b.q: Priya runs a bakery in Orange. She starts making each wedding cake to the couple's own design. What is the most likely effect on her performance objectives?
opts: Customisation improves, but cost per cake may rise
Low cost improves, but customisation falls
Speed improves, but quality may fall
Flexibility falls, but customisation also falls
b.why: Designing each cake for the couple is customisation, and it often takes more time and skill, so cost per cake may rise. The second option reverses the effect: custom work does not usually lower cost.
b.clue: Think about what extra work a one-off design needs.

b.best: Customisation improves, but cost per cake may rise

problems.detail: The clue 'The focus is on keeping a promise, not on how fast' rules out Speed, the only tempting distractor. Flexibility and Customisation are clearly wrong, so the clue all but hands students Dependability.
